### Step 2: 2-adic valuation forces $p \geq 2^{1989}-1$

Compute $v_2(1998!) = \lfloor 1998/2\rfloor + \lfloor 1998/4\rfloor + \cdots = 999+499+249+124+62+31+15+7+3+1 = 1990$.

Since $a$ is even, $v_2(a^{2016}) \geq 2016 > 1990$. From $a^{2016} - 1998! = p^{1998}-1$:

$$v_2(p^{1998}-1) = v_2(a^{2016}-1998!) = \min(2016, 1990) = 1990.$$

By the Lifting the Exponent Lemma (odd $p$, even exponent $1998 = 2\cdot 999$):

$$v_2(p^{1998}-1) = v_2(p-1)+v_2(p+1)+v_2(1998)-1 = v_2(p-1)+v_2(p+1).$$

Since $p$ is odd, $p-1$ and $p+1$ are consecutive even numbers: one has $v_2=1$, the other $v_2\geq 2$. For the sum to be $1990$, the larger has $v_2 = 1989$, so $2^{1989}\mid(p-1)$ or $2^{1989}\mid(p+1)$. Therefore:

$$p \geq 2^{1989}-1 \geq 2^{1988}.$$

### Step 3: Size comparison — contradiction

$$X^{18} - Y^{18} = 1998! - 1.$$

Since $1998! > 1$, we get $X > Y$. If $X \neq Y$, then $X \geq Y+1$ (integers), and:

$$1998! - 1 = (X-Y)\bigl(X^{17}+X^{16}Y+\cdots+Y^{17}\bigr) \geq 1 \cdot Y^{17} = p^{1887}.$$

**Upper bound on $1998!$:** $1998! < 1998^{1998} < 2048^{1998} = 2^{11 \cdot 1998} = 2^{21{,}978}$.

Since $3{,}751{,}356 \gg 21{,}978$:

$$p^{1887} \geq 2^{3{,}751{,}356} > 2^{21{,}978} > 1998! > 1998!-1,$$

contradicting $1998!-1 \geq p^{1887}$.

Therefore $X = Y$, i.e., $a^{112} = p^{111}$, giving $a^{2016} = p^{1998}$ and thus $1998! = 1$ — a contradiction.

### Conclusion
